# Payara Community Code of Conduct

Payara Discussions is where the Payara community asks questions, shares ideas and helps each other. Everyone is welcome, from first-time users to long-time contributors.

This Code of Conduct applies to everything in the Payara repositories on GitHub: Discussions, Issues and pull requests.

The short version: be kind, post in the right place, and help where you can.

## Be kind

Treat this space with the same respect you would give a public park.

- Be civil. Disagreeing is fine, but criticise ideas, not people.
- No name-calling, swearing, personal attacks, or harassment of any kind.
- Respond to what a post says, not the tone you read into it.
- Assume good intent. Many people here are still learning Payara and Jakarta EE.
- Be welcoming to newcomers.

## Keep it tidy

- Search first. Your question may already be answered in Discussions, Issues or the [Payara documentation](https://docs.azul.com/payara-community/).
- Choose the right category for your post.
- One topic per discussion. Please don't post the same thing in several places.
- Use a 👍 reaction instead of "+1" or "me too" comments.
- Stay on topic. If a conversation moves in a new direction, start a new discussion and link back.
- Never post passwords, API keys, licence keys or customer data. Remove them from logs and config files first.
- Only share content you have the right to share. Nothing that helps break the law or someone's licence.
- No advertising or promotion of unrelated products or services. Sharing something relevant to Payara is welcome.
- Please post in English, so everyone in the community can follow and help.

## Help each other

Discussions works best when users help users. Anyone can answer.

- Be patient and explain your reasoning, not just the fix.
- If a reply solves your problem, mark it as the answer so others can find it.
- If you solve it yourself, post what worked.
- Give a 👍 to helpful answers, and say thank you.

## Moderation

Maintainers may edit, move, lock or delete posts and comments that break these guidelines, are spam, or are off topic. Repeated or serious breaches may lead to a block from the Payara organisation on GitHub.

If you see something that doesn't belong, use GitHub's report option on the post, or contact a maintainer. To raise a concern privately, email community@payara.fish.
